utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, exactly, but the witness was saying the truth, and he signed the truth, and I confirmed that in his presence. If now the accused says that it is untrue, then I have betrayed my witness --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the right to say that it is untrue and you have no right to protest --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the right to react.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, you don't have the right. You -- and don't speak about the truth because you're not interested in the truth. You have no relation with the truth. You are a stranger to the truth. Who are you to worry about the truth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, Mr. Seselj, you should not behave this way. Counsel is defending his own professional honour, and he's saying two things. First of all, he confirms what Mr. Marcussen has said and the counsel says my client is telling the truth. That is the truth -- the truth the client has told him and he thinks it is so. Now, you may be of a different opinion. This is not the reason why you should contest the -- what he is saying, the counsel. If he says he saw in Zvornik three cars, the counsel thinks he saw three cars. Maybe he was wrong, maybe there were ten cars. All right. So, Mr. Tomic, please sit down. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what do I care what this attorney thinks and what do you care? It's for him to protect the witness from incriminating himself by giving an answer and that's all. Don't let him do that. I'm not interested in his opinion at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. There is a small legal problem and you are an expert in legal matters and you know better than anybody that when the witness has been heard by the Prosecution counsel was present. You know that. Therefore, everything which has been said by the witness to the Prosecutor was done in the presence of the counsel who was protecting the interests of the witness. Now you've just said: Yes, but the witness didn't say the truth and so on. So therefore, and justly so, the counsel is asking: What is my role in that? So he intervenes. Now you may think the witness made a mistake or said something which was false. You ask him without involving the counsel who did his job.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He must not react, Your Honour. He is not the witness's witness. He must not react to that. I will repeat a hundred times that the witness isn't saying the truth, and it's for him to remain silent or you should throw him out of the courtroom. That's the only correct solution. He cannot interrupt me when I say -- when I put to the witness that he's not saying the truth or when I'm saying you're lying or you're inventing things, and then he's jumping up. He has no right to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: May I suggest that you leave it to the Judges to rule what is going on in this courtroom. I think we should stop this discussion, and I would invite you to move on in your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, Judge Lattanzi told counsel that he should intervene only in a certain domain. So everybody agrees, everybody's understood. But at a certain moment counsel took the floor because he considered that his professional honour was being questioned. It's as if you were insulting the witness because he doesn't agree. So please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I think that Mr. VS-037, you have before you the statement of Colonel Tacic, and I would like to draw your attention to the second paragraph where Colonel Tacic says: Since I commanded the brigade, a brigade which was an armoured brigade and mechanised and didn't have infantry of its own and in Zvornik there weren't enough members of the TO, my brigade needed additional personnel. I asked that we -- we receive reinforcements and, among other things, one unit of volunteers of the Serb Radical Party came. They came from Budanj Potok. You know where that is. They were dressed in JNA uniforms. I bet you had no idea that a hundred or so volunteers of the Serb Radical Party arrived from Belgrade, that they had arrived from Bubanj Potok, and they were uniformed and that they had weapons. You didn't know that, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have that information about who they were or what they were, but I know that Colonel Tacic came to us and asked for additional personnel, but I didn't know that it went through the Serb Radical Party.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You had only heard rumours about some Seselj's men being thereabouts, but on the ground you weren't able to identify them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all dressed the same way. I couldn't tell them apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is there any reason for Colonel Tacic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, Witness, I had wondered about that myself and I put the question to you regarding these volunteers. I asked you how they arrived. And you told me that they were in plain clothes. I even asked you whether they were wearing blue jeans or jackets and you said yes. And suddenly this colonel, who I don't know, is testifying and saying that the volunteers of the Serbian Radical Party arrived in JNA uniform, military battle dress. So there is a difference here. How can you reconcile this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why are we in closed session, if I may ask?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session. Answer my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are speaking about different time-periods. In this statement what's being said is that in early 1992, that is, in February, when there were no conflicts. And I was speaking about volunteers who were arriving in little groups and organised in plain clothes from the 8th or 9th of April, 1992, on. And this is about people dressed in JNA uniforms from Bubanj Potok, they had been trained, prepared, and they completed their training and came to man a unit. And Tacic said to me I have a group of volunteers here, but I don't know who brought them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it correct that those who came to Crisis Staff came there on their own, of their own initiative, sometimes individually in groups of three or four?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they all came on their own in that period and there were no larger groups than what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But somebody could have said to you: I'm a member of the SRS or I fought elsewhere as a member of the SRS. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's possible, but we didn't care. We only -- we needed volunteers to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that Mali Zvornik is just across the bridge; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that the SRS had its Municipal Board there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We won the elections there in May 1992, you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So did the Radicals hold local government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So was there anything more natural for a group of Serb Radicals come from Mali Zvornik to Zvornik and put themselves at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that Janko Lakic was a Radical?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was president of the municipal board in Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did he come from Mali Zvornik on his own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And a number of other Radicals with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised him and another on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you heard of Nenad Jovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that he also came then. I believe that he worked for the police in Mali Zvornik. Where did he work or in the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Nenad Jovic even during my time in the police was with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that some of these SRS members from Mali Zvornik after the 8th of April took up employment in Veliki Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: With the police, the TO, with the municipal services?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and that was normal for Zvornik. And there were reverse cases, people who lived in Zvornik and worked for the police in Mali Zvornik, Rendic, for example.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Used Zvornik to be one town before Yugoslavia became a Federation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it lived as one town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So it was only divided by a bridge over the Drina. So there are a number of SRS members from Mali Zvornik. Isn't it obvious that one thing is the arrival of volunteers from Belgrade, whom I sent as president of the SRS through the JNA to Zvornik, and there are those members of ours who, for patriotic reasons, crossed the Drina from Mali Zvornik to help us. Do you see that distinction clearly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were there members of the SRS from Loznica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that some of them came under the command of Vojislav Jekic to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is there a problem about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received all volunteers gladly because they had come to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you ever heard me on Radio Loznica a few years later saying that some of our volunteers commanded by Vojislav Jekic had gone to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that interview of yours on Radio Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That very interview -- well, and what's the problem with that? And now let's see the third paragraph of the -- Colonel Tacic's paragraph. The members of the SRS were very disciplined and exerted a positive influence on the rest of the men. The volunteers who declared that they were members of the SRS carried out all orders and they never looted or engaged in any criminal activity. They were courageous and they were excellent fighters in the defence. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if that's all correct, but I know that the -- all the volunteers that came to us most -- or, rather, most of them were very good and fair. Unfortunately, volunteers are often mentioned in a negative context. Yes, there were -- there may have been criminal or other in their ranks, but most of them were good fighters.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But in the first stage of the fighting there were also the White Eagles, Arkan's men, and others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Have you heard of a volunteer of the SRS being undisciplined and can you state his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never heard anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you say that any of them was a thief or a looter and can you identify him, mention his name, and do you know that for a fact that he behaved in that manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not while I was in the Crisis Staff, I never heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can you say of any volunteer of the SRS that he killed civilians or prisoners of war, but only if you know his name and know for a fact that he did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know of such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here in this indictment raised against me for political reasons, it is alleged that I am responsible for a series of crimes. But all these crimes were committed from the month of May onwards, and let us now see what Colonel Tacic says about that. First in paragraph 4 he mentions that the Territorial Defence was mobilised and the Mali Zvornik and Loznica municipalities and that there was some volunteers as well as the police reserve units. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So there is no doubt about that. Partial mobilisation of the Territorial Defence and the wartime units of the police. Let us see what Colonel Tacic says about Arkan. On the territory of Zvornik at that time, Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, turned up with some unit of his and without any announcement and without having been invited by the JNA. Actually, he interfered in that armed conflict and only caused problems to the JNA officers. He mistreated some of them and all JNA members could hardly wait to get rid of him. I addressed the General Staff in Belgrade and demanded that Arkan and his men be removed from Zvornik ASAP. I don't remember exactly how many they were, but they were -- but they were 20 to 30 strong. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that I -- my assessment was that they were 20 or 30. Arkan, while he was in Zvornik, he was slapping all members of the Crisis Staff on the face, all the officers were standing in attention when he was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But not Colonel Tacic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Tacic wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Where was his command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was somewhere around Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That is west of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, towards Tuzla, in that direction.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I continue, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute, Mr. Seselj, I'm looking at the clock. Theoretically we're going to have a break because of the tape. We'll make a very short break, ten minutes only, and we will resume -- continue until 7.15, 7.15 p.m., to make sure that you have enough time. But we can't go any further beyond that. There were too many incidents, you raised too many objections and made too many interventions, so we will break for ten minutes only and we will then resume and continue until 7.15.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I will not be able to make full use of my time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You raised a great number of objections and that was a waste of time. We all have to live up to our action. Ten-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Court is back in session. The break was a bit longer than expected because interpreters could not recover in just ten minutes. Interpreting these debates is very tiring because the accused speaks extremely fast, so we extended the break. But because of this we will finish at 7.30 p.m. Mr. Seselj, you have until 7.30. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When you see what Colonel Tacic says about Zeljko Raznatovic, Arkan, then your statement seems a bit surprising, namely, that Arkan commanded the Serb forces in this armed conflict in Zvornik. That's the first thing that surprises me. It was Colonel Tacic who commanded the Serb forces as the commander of the armoured brigade and it was his officers who were engaged in combat operations in the field. Do you think that Arkan was capable of commanding such a large unit at all? Do you think that Arkan has some military knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said on the basis of my impression that he had some 20, 30 men there; secondly, if we were to go into detail, Arkan was in Zvornik twice, once for one hour and the second time two hours and never again --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He slapped people around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, I know about the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He slapped them all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of us from the Crisis Staff were slapped.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did he hit you too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't hit me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He didn't dare to you because you're corpulent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't at the time but he skipped me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why did people let Arkan slap them around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the kind of relationship he had. Then he would slap those that were below him and then others would slap them around, but anyway I saw what the general attitude was. Even Dragan Obrenovic stood at attention when Arkan walked in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So all of you stood at attention, just one military officer and all of you members of the Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was just inertia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So Obrenovic would get up out of inertia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all of us from the Crisis Staff would get up.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that I was engaged in a public clash with Arkan for years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I watched the telecasts from Assembly of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you watch a TV show on TV Politika, there was this TV show when I said to him --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he put stockings more on --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That he put socks more on his head than I put socks on my feet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he didn't dare get up and slap me. So he knew who he could slap and who he could not slap?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, well, he also had some clashes in Zvornik, and when he freed a Muslim from prison and when he ordered that they urgently bring him -- however, the guy walked in with a sub-machine-gun, with an escort of about ten men, and I saw him that he was as small as a mouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Arkan, when he realised that there was danger lurking, just as he stood off in this TV show because I would have beaten him up if he tried to slap me up in that TV studio. Do you believe me -- that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have that experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Or if he drew a weapon, I draw my weapon, and then whoever would get killed. Do you believe that I would never attack anyone with criminal intent, physically or with weapons or in any other way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear of any case when I did anything out of criminal intent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. That's why I'm surprised. Now, the fact that Arkan had to withdraw from Zvornik after two days, are you aware of the fact that it was because of Colonel Tacic's intervention in the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly whose intervention it was, but I know that he left on orders and within 15 minutes they had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They had to leave, otherwise he was threatened with arrest?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time we thought it was betrayal or something; however, they left within 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Towards the end Colonel Tacic says that after the liberation of Zvornik, Kula Grad remained as a stronghold. And then the special unit from Pancevo headed by Lieutenant-Colonel Stupar intervened. You heard of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You mention it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that this unit had Red Berets on their heads?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I think that in your statements to the OTP you confuse this unit of the JNA from Pancevo that had red berets on their heads with this unit of the state security that was later established and that was called the Red Berets. Did you get confused in that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. Zvornik did not have any army stationed there, so it was unusual for us to he see red berets. It was the first time in our lives that we saw red berets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I ought to know this, but I'm not aware that there's a reference in the statement to the Red Berets by this witness, is there?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do I care where it is in the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, you put the question to the witness saying he was confused about his statement. He isn't because there's no reference to the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, you confused him to a maximum yesterday as you showed him those video-clips from Kula, and they could have nothing to do with Zvornik. However, I'm going to get to that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Colonel Tacic says, you know, Kula Grad was a highly fortified stronghold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A rock above Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tanks couldn't do anything; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Artillery nothing. One tank of the JNA was destroyed on the approaches to Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: These fortifications are from the Turkish times or even pre-Turkish times?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fourteenth century.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's a cliff with these stone walls and until this special from Pancevo came, Kula Grad could not fall; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: When Colonel Stupar came, his unit in co-operation with the other units managed to take Kula Grad; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Right. After the liberation of Kula Grad - this is what he wrote, Tacic, that is - the Yugoslav People's Army withdrew from Zvornik and also all the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party. I cannot say whether any individuals stayed. I cannot claim, but the unit of the volunteers of the Serb Radical Party that consisted of brave and disciplined men withdrew together with the Yugoslav People's Army on the 26th of April, 1992. Are you aware of that, that that's when they withdrew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had meetings and we thought that we had been he betrayed and we thought it was a case of betrayal, and in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was on the 8th of May that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a few days later the Army of Republika Srpska was established, and we were told then politically that instead of the JNA there would be the Army of Republika Srpska that would take over.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, Tacic's brigade did leave some weapons to your Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they took some. I know that there was some problems there. I know that the president of the municipality and others went there, asking them not to take weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They took modern tanks and they left the old T-45s?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they took the modern ones, T-84.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, the old ones were very useful to you, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because they had guns of extraordinary quality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you did not remain bare-handed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You know that the ultimatum of the western powers was for the JNA to withdraw from Bosnia-Herzegovina by the 19th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's what the JNA did. After the 26th of April, do you know at all of any situation in the territory of the municipality of Zvornik that Seselj's men or volunteers of the Serb Radical Party are mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they're not being mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Even the White Eagles are not mentioned after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There were a few false witnesses here who claimed that Seselj's men stayed on in May and June as well. Is it correct that from May onwards, that is to say from the 26th of April, in Zvornik there were only three paramilitary formations, Zuco's, that of Pivarski, and that of Niski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say that in that period of time I was no longer on the staff, but since Zvornik is a small town I knew that these -- I heard that these three formations stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You lived there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were sort of in the TO, but they were sort of allowed to have these units that kept these names of Niski, Pivarski, and of Zuco.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Even Gogic's unit did not stay. It joined the police; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Gogic and the team who came from Loznica, very soon they became the police and they had IDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They got jobs in the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some remained even further on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Others got married and even stayed in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: From Gogic's group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Zuco within the Territorial Defence only after the -- was in the Territorial Defence, only after the 26th of April, after the fall of Kula Grad and that he established the establishment of Igor Markovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know who Igor Markovic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A volunteer of theirs who got killed during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He got killed at Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at Kula Grad, so they took his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So there could not have been a unit under that name before the 26th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It was only when Igor Markovic got killed and then to honour him they named the unit after him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did it change its name later into the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The unit of Stojan Pivarski was very small in terms of numbers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know only 10 or 12 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Not more than that? And do you know that Milorad Gogic and Niski were Arkan's men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that they were in the Serb Volunteer Guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Milorad Gogic signed a statement for me that was shown here in the courtroom when another witness was being examined. He said that he was in the Serb volunteer Guards Brigade, that he was one of Arkan's men, and the Prosecutor disclosed to me Niski's statement with his full name and surname stating that he was Arkan's man, he said that himself. You said that Arkan had the habit of leaving behind some of his men who would then rally people together on the ground and that is how they would establish units consisting of his members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how Mauzer's unit came into existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he came to Zvornik with Arkan, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, while I was on the Crisis Staff he was there about 20 times with Arkan and with part of his team.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that this Mauzer afterwards was the vice-president of Zoran Djindjic's party and the president of Djindjic's party for Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a generally known thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That's how he ran in the election?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he was deputy minister of the interior for a while?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either deputy minister or assistant minister, but in Dodik's first government he was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Afterwards, he was killed in a mafia show-down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he got killed, but I don't know the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that in the first parliamentary elections in 1996 in Republika Srpska Arkan's party also ran?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the OSCE, the Organisation for Security and Co-Operation in Europe, or rather, their mission in Bosnia-Herzegovina paid the election campaign costs equally to all political parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's in accordance with the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the OSCE mission gave Arkan's party that amount of money of 300 or 400.000 Deutschemark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those were the first elections after the war.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that the officials of Arkan's party took that money to Arkan immediately in plastic bags in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. But I know about that and the OSCE financed Arkan's party and that is a generally known fact. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Slow down, both of you, please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have very little time left and I have so many questions. I told you that this is an invaluable witness for me. He is from Zvornik. He knows a lot and I want to deal with all of these details with him. That's why I'm hurrying.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, in this indictment - and I claim that it is a false indictment, that's the one that was issued against me - various crimes are being ascribed to me. They say that during the fighting for Zvornik in Zvornik 200 Muslims were killed. Could that be true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is not correct. I think that the service who worked there on the clearing up the terrain, that they're assessment was that it was 10 or 12 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's the information that we received on the Crisis Staff and that they were buried, those who were identified. As for the others, well they were buried as NN persons, persons unknown, and buried at the Zvornik cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: What about the Serb casualties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the first days of the fighting, two I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Or four perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that on that first day of the conflict a group of Arkan's men headed by Arkan himself in the settlement of Hrid took out of cellars 20 Muslim civilians, men, and they were executed on the spot before their very own wives and children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A day before the attack there was this fuse from a hand-grenade that injured me, so I did not take part directly in the fighting for Zvornik, but I didn't hear of that story.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, if I tell you that a Muslim woman was here, she was a protected witness so I cannot give you her name, and that she was an eye-witness to the effect that Arkan's men executed, shot dead 20 Muslim men and they killed her husband and two sons according to her testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any direct knowledge about that, but I imagine it's true if she said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I would like to hear your opinion on how convincing you find her statement. What she said here -- I'm not going to quote her verbatim but I'm going to present the gist of what she said --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: It is not for the accused to ask this witness to pass judgement on the credibility or reliability of the evidence of another witness. That is clearly interfering with the job of Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, but the accused is allowed through this witness to make a number of checks relating to a previous statement made by another witness without challenging anyone. Continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the last question of the accused is quite strange, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I think maybe part of the -- part of the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are the kind of questions I like best.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I -- there might have been something missing in the transcript, I'm not sure, but what I heard was he was going to ask the witness about the correctness of some of the facts set out and that is commenting on the evidence of the witness. If he has specific questions about the events, although the witness has said he has no specific knowledge of it, he can ask those questions. I don't know how the witness can answer when he has twice confirmed that he doesn't know. The accused should move on to another area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he can have knowledge about the bad relations between the so-called Seselj's men and Arkan's men, and I'm going to ask him about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that among -- between the volunteers of the SRS on the one hand and Arkan's men and the other's men there was a sort of enmity that we never wanted to go into action together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, that they couldn't get along with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the volunteers of the SRS ever accept Arkan's commands?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you see, and this witness was speaking along these lines. He -- she spoke about this execution incident. She was sore and she showed hostility towards me and all Serbs, et cetera. But she said something very interesting, too. When the Arkan's men executed these men, the women and children were in an extremely difficult situation of uncertainty, et cetera. They -- she says that Seselj's men had taken care of them, put them up in the municipality building, and comforted them, saying: Don't be afraid, we're not like Arkan's men, we're Seselj's men, we're different. Don't be afraid, you're not in danger. Something along those lines. That's what she said. Is that convincing to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that is so if the woman said as much that it's possible the way -- it was that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: She mentioned one more detail. She said that one of the -- of Seselj's men approached a shop, broke the shop window with a stone, took some sweets out, and distributed them to Muslim children --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If Judge Lattanzi dislikes this question, I'll withdraw it. Let's move on, so as not to include Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The problem is that the witness said that he had been injured and he wasn't there. So we're wasting time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. If I'm wasting time, let's not go into how much time Mr. Marcussen has wasted.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And this indictment, which I insist is false, murder -- the murder of 750 Muslims in the secondary school at Karakaj is mentioned. Have you heard of that murder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were there really 750?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how many they were, but they were very many.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: How -- when did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In late June or early July 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, well they split them up. I'm not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, they singled out Grujic and Popovic, and they were tried separately.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: One was from Niski's unit and another from the Yellow Wasps, do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, another indictment was issued. It's about Zvornik and the incidents at Kozluk and Celopek Donji, and that's the first-instance when some people were convicted. And then another indictment was issued only about this secondary technical school at Karakaj which I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I'm no longer sure what the position is, but it was my understanding that we had been in closed session earlier when -- or in private session when we had been discussing the witness as a -- this witness as [overlapping speakers] in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in public session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, sorry, but earlier when these things have come up we have been in private session, so I wonder whether we do not need to redact. If I could just -- if the accused --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing needs to be revised. You're only taking up my time and you're doing it on purpose. What do you want to achieve ? I believe that the Bench should forbid you such interventions. I have said nothing that could reveal the identity of this witness. I asked him whether he knows that I was involved in a concrete criminal act, if I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... continue, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, the Chamber has been apprised of a judgement made in Belgrade. I think this judgement is still being translated. As soon as it is translated, the Chamber will peruse it with great attention thanks to the questions asked by the accused and by the answers of the witness we learned two things which I didn't know. First of all, there was a disjoinder for two persons, two individuals. The names have disappeared from the transcript. And one hears thanks to the witness - and I thank the witness - that there has been another indictment concerning only Karakaj, what we didn't know and which the Prosecution hadn't told us about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe we have provided these records to the Trial Chamber. But the issue is at paragraph -- in page 53, line 2, what I think should be redacted is that the witness says that he -- no, sorry, that's not where it is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Why don't you let this confused Mr. Marcussen to come --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: The only issue is that --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to recover --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this redaction of one word in the transcript cost me 15 to 20 minutes in this trial, and the Prosecutor does it deliberately. Because if one word is redacted, those who are preparing the broadcasting, that is, the transmission, they redact 15 to 20 minutes. If I can't a public trial, I don't want to take part at all. More than half the witnesses here have protective measures. I do not trust this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- Tribunal. I'm only interested in this trial if I can take part publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... technical reason when there is one minute that disappears from the transcript, the broadcast in Belgrade -- there are 20 minutes which are squeezed. So be careful when you ask a question. You can say there is a risk of having it redacted. So just think about the problem. Right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I phrase my questions very carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In this indictment I am stated as the person responsible for this crime at Celopek, where prisoners were tortured. Have you heard of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was general knowledge. Everybody in Zvornik heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did the events there have anything to do with the volunteers of the SRS or me personally as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was involved in that trial, as I said, and some people were convicted of these crimes, but neither you nor your party were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The indictment goes on to say that on the 30th of May the prisoners from the brickworks were taken over, that those prisoners were used to loot civil property in Zvornik, that is, that they looted for somebody else. Has that anything to do with the volunteers of the SRS or me personally?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or maybe we should terminate this cross-examination because this doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, nobody understood it properly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nobody understood, Mr. President. I am asking questions about the counts of the indictment. Whether the witness heard about those crimes and whether those crimes can be connected with me. That -- my questions were about Zvornik. I never even indicated a link with another trial before the witness himself made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, listen, I believe -- maybe I'm wrong but maybe Mr. Marcussen was wrong too, but we got the impression that you were asking questions concerning the Belgrade trial. Now you tell us you didn't so proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I mentioned the demolishing of mosques. When were the Zvornik mosques demolished?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May or June.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: None was demolished during the fighting for Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Was the demolishing of any of Zvornik's mosques something that can be -- something between which a connection can be made with me or my -- the -- my volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But did the Muslims demolish Orthodox churches in the Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you know that the Muslim forces demolished the St. Mary's church at Velim [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that the Muslim forces demolished the Orthodox church of St. Martar [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Muslim forces demolished the Orthodox church in Lijesce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lijesce, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Muslim forces demolished a Serbian Orthodox church of St. Lazarus of Serbia at Rastosnica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Muslim forces demolished the Serbian Orthodox church of the descent of the holy spirit at Lijesce?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at Lijesce.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So there were two churches at Lijesce. Do you know that Muslim forces demolished the Serbian Orthodox church of St. Ilija at Setici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they damaged it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but damaged it badly; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So the demolishing of religious buildings was something that both sides did, so it was like an eye for an eye?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Let's now tackle another interesting question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Mr. Seselj asked you to confirm that several religious monuments, Orthodox, were destroyed and you confirmed this. But you added "an eye for an eye," which means that the Serbs have also destroyed mosques?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that was certain reciprocity involved.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that was all in the territory of the municipality of Zemun. Some Serbs demolished mosques and on the other hand some Muslims demolished Orthodox churches.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Judges, it's about who controlled which territories. In Serb-controlled territories not one Muslim religious building remained standing and it was similar on the other side too.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I continue? I'm already panicking for reasons of time. I haven't gone through a third of what I wanted to cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I suppose that you heard because you mentioned so in some of your statements that a day or two before armed conflict broke out the Muslim forces stopped a car with Belgrade licence plates and in that car there were four soldiers in JNA uniforms but without insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Milorad Lukovic, Legija, was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Later he was Arkan's man and even later a colonel of --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, the Red Berets of the police. And the other was the -- was Colonel Vuckovic called Zuco, the commander of the Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was also his brother nicknamed Repic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And that the fourth man was Miroslav Bogdanovic from Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know why they came to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They also came as volunteers, to assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you don't know about this? I showed here statements by Milorad Lukovic, Legija, which he gave to my Defence team and also statements of Zuco, and in there they had explained that they had come to Zvornik pursuant to order from Nedjo Boskovic, have you heard of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At that time he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: General of the intelligence service of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I think that back then he still had the rank of lieutenant-colonel and in May he became general. He was head of security service of the JNA within the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That they had come with a task with arrest Pusula?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is he from Rasula [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The military security service had information that Pusula was smuggling weapons and selling them to Serbs and Muslims. Did you have such information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They received the task to arrest him and take him to Belgrade take him into custody, and they received that assignment directly from Nedjo Boskovic, and then they were arrested by Muslim policemen and that's how you know about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you've heard of Fadil Mujic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I worked with Fadil Mujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was also one of police executives in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was head of the crime investigations department at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you he hear when Muslims arrested these four at the barricades, that they beat them severely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Miroslav Bogdanovic was beaten to such an extent that he had to be taken to Belgrade for treatment. He didn't even remain in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I just happen to know him because sometime that year he became a member of the Serbian Radical Party, but he wasn't a member when he arrived in Zvornik. Fadil Mujic believed that these were Arkan's men; correct? You don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And do you know that Fadil Mujic stated this, that after the four men were arrested sometime at around 1300 hours he received a phone call from Nedjo Boskovic from Belgrade personally, at that time he was lieutenant-colonel and later on became general?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that from Fadil Mujic that evening when he released them he called me and he told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Nedjo Boskovic called him twice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Fadil confirmed that to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He claimed that those people were military policemen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what he told me on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that Fadil Mujic arranged with Vojislav Jekic to release these men, right, and that in return Jekic would help Mujic to leave Yugoslavia via Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They knew each other well. They went to the same university in Skopje --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They were friends?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were friends, and their houses are nearby so they are neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So he said to him release these men and we will let you leave Yugoslavia via Serbia. Is that how it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did Mujic leave the country via Serbia, and did he go abroad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he and the family left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So both he and the family left via Serbia owing to the fact that he had released these four because it's questionable whether they would have let him pass otherwise. Wasn't that the agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was his agreement with Jekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. So we've clarified that. Why was this important for me? Because there was some witnesses who claimed that on these people they found membership cards of the Serbian Radical Party. Did you ever hear of them having our party IDs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they were released I was present at the Jezero hotel in Mali Zvornik because I had my leg bandaged and I was there. I know that Legija immediately joined Arkan's unit and that he was their member.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Legija did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So he joined Arkan's unit in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately. He said there was some danger, that Zvornik would be attacked, and I was still at the SUP and he gathered us there. There was some 50 policemen there and he came with Arkan's team and he said that some -- he was their officer. I forgot what rank he held at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Zuco set up his unit after the 26th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And I think that somewhere you stated that he had already taken part with Yellow Wasps in fighting for Zvornik. Did you state that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Yellow Wasps didn't exist at the time, but at the time I didn't really care much about these time references. When I say that Zuco participated in liberating Zvornik -- but at the time he wasn't Zuco, he was Vojan Vuckovic, and it was only after Goran Markovic was killed that they set up this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But in combat for Kula Grad Zuco held no command position; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely because the JNA fought there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And if he did take any part he could have done it only as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You stated that in April of 1992 Biljana Plavsic came to Zvornik twice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: She came a day or two before this armed showdown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: She held a meeting with the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She visited the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And the Crisis Staff talked to her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did she then give a proposal that Arkan be called to come from Bijeljina to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: She had already arrived -- Arkan had a unit stationed there. He went from Bijeljina to Mali Zvornik in Serbia, to a hotel called Rada and he was up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let's take it step by step. You went to Bijeljina after the departure of Biljana Plavsic; am I right? First Biljana Plavsic came to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And it was only then that you went to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then you escorted Rada -- Arkan to Rada?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Arkan wasn't there the whole time. He was just in Bijeljina and he said my team was there, and then Major Pejic took them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There were about 20 to 30 people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So I'm right. So first Biljana Plavsic came to Zvornik and then you went to Bijeljina to fetch Arkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then Arkan's men came to Rada?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember in that meeting of the Crisis Staff Biljana Plavsic proposed or demanded that Arkan be invited to come to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present but I heard from my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you hear that she asked that Arkan be brought there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You heard it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from the people who attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You heard it reliably?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And you heard that she was on very good terms with him in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was some photographs with her kissing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, on TV?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I'm not sure on what terms they were, but yes I saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In Zvornik you thought that Arkan represented some power?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then you were in for an unpleasant surprise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he didn't spend much time in Zvornik, only two or three hours, and his unit wasn't there for a long time either. But as fighters they were excellent fighters but we had bad experience with them in the sense that he had a very bad attitude towards the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Uh-huh. And then he mistreated you there, he slapped some people around, beat some people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So you practically got yourself into trouble by inviting him? Now looking back it would have been better if he hadn't come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, looking back at it today it would have been better if nothing happened, we would have all been much happier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, you're giving me a very general answer. I asked for a more specific answer. Looking at it today, it would have been much better for everybody if Arkan hadn't come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for everybody, including himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: At least this first big crime would not have happened. And when this crime did take place in the Hrid settlement, a special team of the JNA came from Belgrade - do you remember that? - led by Zoran Stankovic who was a colonel at the time, later a general and a minister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard of that. He's a pathologist from the military medical academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, and they conducted exhumations and pathological processing or autopsy of all corpses of victims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: We had Zoran Stankovic testify here in open session. So the JNA wanted to investigate these crimes; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was an investigation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, the investigation was interrupted due to the withdrawal of JNA from Bosnia-Herzegovina and nobody else was prepared to continue with investigations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: While the JNA was in the territory of Zvornik, every crime was investigated; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't get involved into that. I just know that they conducted on-site investigations related to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Now, let us make a minor digression. Yesterday, the Prosecutor showed you the video footage of the ceremony in Kula of the Red Berets from 1997 I guess. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was played on TV hundreds of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes, but then the Prosecutor tendered into evidence the entire transcript, which we didn't hear here. And that transcript contains a speech. I have to give you an introductory explanation, a speech by Franko Simatovic, Frenki, where he boasts by giving examples of wartime successes of the unit, mentioning Zvornik as well. According to what you know, did that unit, special unit of the state security of Serbia, the so-called Red Berets, did it ever come to the territory of Zvornik during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They never came there with their unit. It's just that I had this incident with Kostic, I had this contact with him. And now, whether he was a member of that unit, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let me remind you, Kostic was from Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Before the outbreak of the war he came to Zvornik. His parents were from Zvornik and he was perhaps born there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was born in Mali Zvornik, in Velika Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So he came there from Dalina [phoen] from the Serbian Krajina, where he was a highly placed police official? I'm doing this to assist you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he came there several times and there was this logistical assistance that I explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So he assisted you regarding this logistics, so he had some influence, he had some clout. And on one occasion he ensured weapons from the JNA depot in Dalina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Were all of the weapons from the JNA depot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, where else it could have come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. But you undoubtedly remember that in early 1991 the General Staff of the armed forces issued an order that the JNA was to take over all depots of TO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so as to prevent any abuse by republican organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know how much Muslim officials in Zvornik complained about those depots, asking that the JNA return weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the greatest political problem at the local level.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And JNA refused to return it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then later on when it was needed to defend territorial integrity of the country these weapons were placed at your disposal. Rade Kostic brought those weapons from Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Did you accompany him, did you go with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. That's important because I don't want anybody to think that those weapons came from Serbia. Now, Frenki gave this statement. You know, he and I are here in jail together in the same block, and when I asked him he said that somebody else wrote that speech for him. And we have no trace nor does the Prosecution have any trace that those Red Berets did indeed stay in the territory of Zvornik. Let me ask you this now: You know that Rade Kostic was killed in 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you know that he died as a volunteer in the military formations of Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Ramic [phoen] Brdo near Kladusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Near Kladusa. So he was a volunteer in a Muslim army of Fikret Abdic; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at that time the Serbian forces of Krajina and Abdic fought together.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They had an alliance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Because Fikret Abdic was not a fundamentalist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And he wanted to coexist with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He also wanted to coexist with Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On TV during the war we saw him visiting Milosevic in Belgrade and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But he educated -- he wanted Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was his main idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it true that Rade Kostic died as a hero, as a fighter of Fikret Abdic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I would like to ask if the accused could point us to the place in Frenki's speech where he mentions Zvornik. I have just been looking and he mentioned a whole number of locations, but I cannot see Zvornik being mentioned. And as these propositions are being put through the witness for the witness to agree with, I think this illustrative of the problems of the kind of examination that's going on. But maybe I am wrong and maybe the accused actually is referring to some specific place in the speech he is mentioning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I will simply state for the record that Mr. Marcussen fell into a trap, and could he now explain to us why this transcript was admitted into evidence and what it has to do with this trial and with Zvornik, if Mr. Marcussen could please explain this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I should be most happy to if the accused will have me use time on that today, but I think the accused may want to re-consider that. The real issue is that propositions are being put to a witness as if they come from a document and they are actually not in the document and the witness is made to agree to it. Now, in any event the probative value of propositions being put to a witness and a witness agreeing with them is minimal but this is highly problematic, and the accused is refusing to tell us where this proposition is. That's my simple point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, I'm deliberately bringing out here things that have minimal evidential value, but on the other hand I'm demonstrating what can be achieved by leading questions. And all three interviews of yours actually prompted witness to give some answers, importance of which he was not aware at the time. So what do you want now? You're just wasting my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, when it comes to Arkan you confirmed to me that Biljana Plavsic came to Zvornik before the armed showdown and that she was the first one to propose that Arkan be brought to Zvornik; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I heard that from my colleagues from the Crisis Staff. I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. So you heard of a man called Perisa Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know the man called Perisa Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Prosecution gave me a document -- the Prosecution, don't think that I invented this document. They gave me a statement by Perisa Ivanovic from the 16th of July, 2003. I was given this under Article 68(i) as potentially exculpatory material. I will only ask you now whether two or three statements from that statement by Perisa Ivanovic are correct. This is what Perisa Ivanovic claims: At the Crisis Staff they used to say that Arkan needs to come to Zvornik and that we need to pay him for that. Was this discussed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never, at least not in my presence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. So he also says this: They said that somebody would need to pay him for that and that the money needs to be paid out from a company called Ekonomija. It was a company in Zvornik which was quite a wealthy one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I think they were speaking about these contributions and fund-raising, that the Muslims did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And there was a fire there in the factory producing leather and that it was quite an extensive damage. And then he goes on to say, he mentions three names, including yours, I won't mention any of them --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Perisa is a man who was a simple man at a rather low level. He had no access to the Crisis Staff, and I think he mixed up things. There was some talk of paying Arkan, but it was discussed in the context of buying jeeps for his unit. But that was some time later, not in 1990-something, but, yes, just to make it clear there was some discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Arkan never fought for free anywhere?
