utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I have to confess that we never paid him anything at least according to what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I believe you, but this is what Perisa Ivanovic goes on to say. He says the money was collected from local companies and Arkan was paid by and then he mentions your name. This is what Perisa claims and I received this from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one needs to know Perisa. We need to call him here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm not going to call him Perisa. Let the Prosecution bring him here. This is something that I received from the Prosecution, because the Prosecution gives you suggestions in order to receive certain answers from you and then they swamp me with material. This is the methodology. And now this is what he also says: I heard from Brano Grujic that the payment was made in Radaljska Banja where there was a hotel and that you negotiated with Arkan and that you brought him to Zvornik. It is true that you brought him to Zvornik; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Now, bringing him to Zvornik, that can be interpreted in different ways, have different meanings.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You didn't tie him up and drag him in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I brought him because Rade Kostic told me to go and fetch him.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However, I have a statement of yours here to the effect that Rade Kostic warned you that Arkan was a criminal and that you shouldn't have any business with him. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, he tried in the local settings where he was to create units like Mauzer's, et cetera, and that is what I was offered in Zvornik. Since I knew Rade Kostic as a man I trusted, he told me that I should not communicate with the type of -- I had not even known of him. I heard about him only two days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Biljana Plavsic was an authority for all of you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Biljana was a member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina on behalf of the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The OTP has a document showing that Biljana Plavsic is inviting me and Arkan and Mirko Jovic to send volunteers. Of course, I never responded to that call but -- because I was never on good terms with Biljana, but the Prosecution sent this anyway. Okay, there are some other things I want to check through this dialogue with you. You heard of a certain Dragan Gotovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He's a lawyer; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he works as a lawyer now. He was a prosecutor before.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was born in 1995 [as interpreted], a year younger than me. I think I remember him from university.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Studied in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He was mobilised at the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The JNA mobilised him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, all JNA officers were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Yes. And he was interviewed here or there -- never mind, by investigators from The Hague. And at one point in this interview that was disclosed to me as public material by the OTP, there is this Mitford-Burgess. There is a name that had two functions at the time. That is a name that had direct responsibility over persons who committed crimes. That name is your name. Dragan Gotovac, not only on paper but people told us that it was your responsibility. We do not have any other response for anyone who had responsibility and power. This has to do with the crime in Drinjaca. So this is a local person; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Gotovac is an eminent lawyer in Zvornik. He was mobilised in the beginning of the war, but I don't think he was at Drinjaca. I think he was at a different zone. I think that he was an artillery man.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: He had a squad of mortars; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Tell me, did you have that kind of thing happen to you, that the investigators of the OTP throw something into your face and then you try to find your way through all of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had a fair and correct relationship with them, but perhaps sometimes I did not pay enough attention to all of this. You see how many questions there are over a short period of time. It's impossible to pay that attention to everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: We need to be in private session if we are to reveal -- it might be necessary to reveal to the witness who had been interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor but that is not something that should be in public and is also -- well, it's even more so considering that it's being referred to as a suspect interview. Also, I think we should avoid mentioning employees of the OTP in public.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges, the OTP did not submit this to me as confidential material but as public material according to Rule 68(i). They typed the transcript and translated it into the Serbian language and submitted it to me. I don't want to go into private session. If I cannot discuss this in public session, I give up on it and we move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Continue, otherwise the Chamber will redact. So you have to make a difference between a witness and a suspect it's important --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Come on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a witness and not mention that he was a suspect and then you wouldn't have run into a problem. Saying that it's also a -- this person is also a suspect can create trouble in the place where this person lives and there's no need for that. Just say a witness said but don't say a witness who is a suspect. Don't say that. But now continue and refrain from doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They suspected this man committed murders at the technical school in Karakaj and what happened in Bijeljina Klanica, you heard about that. And then at one point Bernard O'Donnell says to him: According to the information that we received until now, you are the person who is the most responsible for these men. So they suspect many people, locals from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That case was clarified and it has nothing to do with Petko Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But it had been ascribed to him. So then out of all of these suspects, not to mention all of them so that they don't take up our time with these requests for going into closed session. And finally when they got through all of that, when they accused different persons of these crimes, then they finally reduced the indictment to me only. Isn't that a bit strange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I was not in Zvornik at all when these crimes took place and volunteers of the Serb Radical Party weren't there either. Yesterday you mentioned that you were at my rally in Mali Zvornik. You said that this rally had to be held before July 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: July 1991 is a parameter for me because that's when I joined the police. I know that I didn't come as an active-duty policeman. I came as a civilian. So that must be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If I tell you that it was the beginning of August 1990?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is very possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you remember that there was an incident that happened at the rally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, because the police prepared that incident for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The police did? That is news for me. Who prepared that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess they didn't like rallies like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oh, they didn't like Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or the change in the system, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They didn't like the abolition of the communist order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And they brought Muslims mostly and there were a few Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: To throw stones at us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they brought a truckful of rocks to be thrown.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: They brought a truckful of rocks to be thrown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Do you agree that it was in August 1990?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the date but it -- certainly that's a plausible date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: There was a Prosecution witness here who claimed that the rally took place in March 1992, just before the armed conflict in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can guarantee 1 billion per cent that this had to be before July 1991, 1 billion per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, just a moment, I'll take some of Mr. Seselj's time but this is an extremely important element. The Prosecution is saying that there was a rally in March 1992 and then the Prosecution connects everything that happened after that day to this meeting and you were in the police at the time. If there had been such a rally in March 1992, rally organised by Mr. Seselj, you would have known about it, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'd have to know because I would be involved, but I can guarantee 1 billion per cent, I bet you my entire property. You can ask anyone in the street in Zvornik. I tell you I guarantee that. I don't know the exact date but I hadn't been working at the police yet and I attended the rally as a civilian, and I guarantee it was before July 1991, 1 billion per cent sure, there's no dilemma.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, no one is challenging that a rally was held in August 1990; however, we would like to know whether there was another rally held in March or April 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I would have known that with 100 per cent certainty if we're talking about a rally in Mali Zvornik. It is certain that no other rally was held.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: You remember that already then there were many people under arms in March 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Is it possible to have that kind of incident when people are armed to the teeth, is it possible to have this kind of incident without bloodshed, to have someone throw rocks at me and my associates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all of us who know about this and who live there, I mean it's absolutely impossible. There is not even a theoretical chance of this kind of rally being held on the eve of the war. I would have known that for sure and that would have been my professional duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Here in this court a man spoke about you. I'm not going to mention his name. I'm just going to present a particular piece of information. He said that you had been threatened by The Hague OTP that you would be indicted and that they extorted a large amount of money from you so that you would not be indicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is nebulous, I was never threatened and as for the rest of what you said it's so nebulous that it's not worth discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's in the official transcripts of the Tribunal. I got that from the OTP.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, lots of people come and say all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: A man who said this kind of lie must have lied about other things too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who that is but it is so, so --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judges just for the sake of you knowing about this, I'm not going to mention the name, it was VS-036 in my trial, but later on he was killed in a mafia showdown, so we will not have the opportunity of seeing him here in the courtroom unless the Prosecution makes him appear in some magical way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is what he said, that you were supposed to pay $600.000, to give 300.000 up front and 300.000 within 15 days. Listen to me carefully. I thought it was funny too, but let's see whether it is true. And then one of the Judges from the Trial Chamber - I'm not even going to mention the Judge's name - asked him the following. You said that you found out from a friend that he was negotiating with someone to pay for his freedom and when it was asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Marcussen, maybe I misunderstood something, witness VS-036 would have testified and then got killed? No?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. He --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He never testified here, but he testified in other cases. But he was killed because he was involved in Arkan's assassination. His murder has nothing to do with The Hague Tribunal. He was one of the accomplices in Arkan's killing, and then on this wave of revenge they killed him too. Again, I'm not going to refer to his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: As --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So he was not -- he did not testify in the present case. I wanted to check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: He's the subject of a 92 quater motion, and he was not -- he was not killed in the context of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, thank you to Mr. Marcussen. Now I don't have to worry that even -- that I would be blamed even for his killing, that I'd have to face that indictment too. However, Judges, since this was tendered I believe that this is an opportunity for us to check the credibility of at least one of his statements so that you see who you're dealing with. As far as I know, you haven't agreed to have this dealt with under 92 quater. Is that right, Mr. Marcussen, because I'm not really very well versed in this. The decision is yet to be made; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, after this question that was put by one of the members of the Trial Chamber, can you clarify this who are these people, et cetera, this is what his answer is. This was at a secret session in this other case. The OTP provided me with transcripts of this secret session. It is important for me that you either deny this or confirm this. If you deny it, then you help me challenge the credibility of that witness. I hope you understand now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: I understand why the accused wants to put the question. I do not object to putting the question, but the witness [sic] cannot quote from a closed session or private session testimony in another case without us going into private session as well. So I ask that we move into private session so the accused can put the question, which may be relevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. If I do not mention the witness's name and if I do not mention the trial concerned, the only thing that is mentioned here are the names of The Hague investigators who allegedly extorted money --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, part of a transcript done in closed session cannot be mentioned openly. That's the way it is. So --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I give up on that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... withdraw your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I do now. I don't want to go into any kind of secret session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, there is another man who is a high police official, or rather, was a high police official on the other side of the Drina. I'm not going to mention his name, but you can assume who that person is -- not this person I mentioned just now but very close to that person. He said something that gave me a good laugh. You have a master's degree, don't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In economics.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Can we say in public session where you got your master's degree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got my diploma in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: However can we say where you defended your master's thesis?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the University of Belgrade. I didn't defend my thesis but I passed all my exams.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Oh, in Belgrade, I already see that this is not true. Are you interested in what this person has to say in connection with your master's thesis? I'm not going to mention the name --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it's of interest to you and if it can help you --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It's of interest to me so that we can have a good laugh, but if you don't want to never mind. Whatever you say. See, I'm in a good mood, so --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you choose.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I think that it's going to be rather witty and indicative because that man is also a witness in some other trials, not in my trial but in other trials of The Hague. You've already guessed who this man is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume who it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This is what he told my associates --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry I have to object, but the accused is clearly indicating that he has identified a witness. I don't know whether it's a protected witness in another case, but it's clear that the information he has provided by the witness allow people to guess who the witness is. So I'm sorry that I [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: -- I think we need to redact this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't identified any one witness, absolutely none.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, it has just been put on record that this witness is able to guess who it is. We're all going to have a good laugh, and it's clearly implied that everyone knows who this is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This witness can of course guess who it is, but so what. You, Mr. Marcussen, don't know who I'm speaking about and I'm not going to tell you or the Trial Chamber or the lawyer of this witness. Why shouldn't I say that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, just say that a witness said something about this other witness and that will be enough and that way no one can identify anyone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just re-tell his story, how he introduced this witness to my collaborators. The facts are wrong. This witness studied at Brcko and made his master's study in Belgrade. I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I heard that you wanted to defend your master's thesis in Pristina and before doing so you gave the -- your mentor a Volkswagen Golf and that you -- before he was able to take possession of that Golf you sneaked up to the place where the car was parked and you drove it away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is some truth in that. I did want to defend my master's thesis, but finally I didn't because the war had started, et cetera. And that professor did come to see me afterward. He -- I sold him a car and at a fair price because he was a professor of mine. And it is true that the car disappeared after a few days, but the story goes on that he was a good friend of our ambassador to Bulgaria at the time and the car was returned after ten days or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Well, people tend to add elements to a story. Isn't that part of your nature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we had exercises at the university of such Chinese whispers.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: In the third year of our studies the professor would display an incident in the lecture theatre, and then when he would ask the students to tell what they had seen the stories would all differ among themselves. And that also goes to show how reliable human memory can be after ten or more years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it isn't very reliable.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Now, yesterday the Prosecutor showed you some documents, among which an exert from the Official Gazette of the Republika Srpska. I would like to see it on the ELMO again. I have it here someplace, but perhaps the Prosecutor could give me a hand and provide a copy. These are the so-called strategic goals of the Serbian people. The Prosecutor doesn't want to help me. It was assigned an IT number yesterday, but I refuse to remember numbers. They say that only stupid people remember numbers. You don't want to give me a hand, Prosecutor. Yeah, sure, you're mad at me. I sure would be mad at you if I were you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it's so stupid why should Mr. Marcussen remember the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Well, opposed to certain others who get angry in court --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because I don't have an assistant in the courtroom and he has many. Could you please put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should we -- or are we going to see it on our screens or should we put it on the ELMO? Let's put it on the ELMO. This could be my final question if my time will be up soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you we would stop at 7.30. There are a number of things that need to be taken into account, the interpreters who are working over time and let me tell you also that I have been sitting on this bench since 9.00 a.m. this morning, 9.00 a.m non-stop.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can go on all night.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Let us take a look at this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The Prosecutor tendered this into evidence yesterday and you confirmed that you read this in the Official Gazette of the Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I said that this was general knowledge and that I heard of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: All right. Take a look at the issue of the Official Gazette or the date. Friday, the 26th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And in the alleged decision or the alleged decision reads that this is the People's Assembly of the Republika Srpska, that is the Serbian people of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that it adopted these at the meeting on the 12th of May, 1992. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: So from the 12th of May, 1992, they waited until the 26th of November, 1993, an entire year and a half to publish that document in the Official Gazette. Isn't that incredible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is practice to publish everything in the Official Gazette with as little delay as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Of a few days, eight at most?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the -- in the first issue of the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And something else in the preamble which is -- can't be found in a serious document. The People's Assembly of Republika Srpska of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Isn't that an impossible name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That name was only used before the war, but not during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Take a close look. Is it this very name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this name --

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: This name was never used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was never used.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Initially it was the People's Assembly of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: And then it was changed to the people's Assembly of Republika Srpska; am I completely right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the change took place somewhere early in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: That doesn't matter, but there has never been anything called the People's Assembly of the Republika Srpska of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina; am I completely right or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice that, but this is an illogical name, and I have never seen the Assembly called that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: It is utterly impossible. And what's more, I look at the transcript of that meeting. On the 12th of May, the People's Assembly did not adopt such a decision. It cannot be found in the transcripts. The OTP has all transcripts and yet is unable to find it. Isn't it obvious that this is a fake?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert in fakes or forgeries, but this is illogical. The names, the date of publication, all this is illogical.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: If I say that the Republika Srpska, or rather, its People's Assembly never adopted such strategic objectives, am I right or am I wrong?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VS-037 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really say whether you're right or wrong. I have heard of these strategic decisions, but whether they were published in the newspapers or the Official Gazette -- I heard of these objectives. But I believe that there was ten and not six.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: But this was mentioned in various trials in The Hague, but the Defence teams failed to ask such crucial questions. What can I do if there are miserable people walk through these courtrooms and get long prison sentences? But this was never adopted by the National Assembly and this is now used as evidence against the Serb people and corroboration of the joint criminal enterprise. Here is a prize question for Mr. Marcussen: Who printed this and how come that this was printed without the National Assembly ever adopting such a decision? Perhaps the Chamber could give this homework to Mr. Marcussen until the next session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for giving me so much time, even though I didn't get as much as Mr. Marcussen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Marcussen, the accused says that this document is a forgery because the text under 386, because of the date it bears and the formulae cannot be an authentic document. The investigations made will establish that on the 12th of May, 1992, there was never such a thing as this meeting. So I can't conclude anything more than what has been said --

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may propose --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Such a decision was never adopted. Maybe there was a session of the Assembly, but such a decision cannot be found anywhere in the transcripts of the National Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: And yesterday -- Your Honours, yesterday the accused asked for the minutes of this session and -- I mean, he obviously knew about it because it is exhibit 65 ter number 1297. I'm not going to make submissions about the contents of this, but I would in light of what has been said today and also what was said about the document yesterday suggest that we move that into evidence as well, and I move for the admission of the document. It's the minutes of the 12 May 1992 Assembly that we have been discussing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let Mr. Marcussen show us the page which contains this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARCUSSEN
utterances.text: This is a -- and has been an issue in many trials here. I'm not going to make that. We can make submissions about all this when the appropriate time comes at the end of the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. The Chamber is seized of your request. We noted carefully what has been said by Mr. Seselj on the fact that the transcript of the Assembly of the 12th of May, 1992, does not correspond to this text adopted. So the conclusion would be that it would be a forgery which would then have been put into a publication. This gives the idea to have had a whole organisation and system to actually include in an Official Gazette such a document. The Chamber is going to think about this. Witness, your -- Witness, you have now finished your testimony --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... conspiracy and I want my copy back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which copy?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just want my copy of the document back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're going to have it back. You can have it back. There is no plot, no intention of confiscating a document from you. Now, Witness, thank you. I also thank you -- I also thank Mr. Tomic for having been present. I wish you a nice trip home. As we know, if the next witness comes we will meet again next week, Tuesday, and we will have two sessions in the morning at 9.00. Thank you all. Before we leave the courtroom, Mr. Witness, wait until the blinds have been lowered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 19th day of January, 2010 at 9.00 a.m. 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.39 p.m.
